algorithm: 2B-parameter flow-matching diffusion transformer (H-RDT), pretrained on EgoDex human hand-pose trajectories then fine-tuned per robot embodiment by reinitializing the state/action adaptors and action decoder
hand: parallel-jaw / 2-jaw grippers at deployment (Aloha-Agilex, ARX5, Franka-Panda, UR5+UMI); no dexterous hand deployed, though pretraining action space includes bimanual fingertip positions from EgoDex
arm: dual-arm Piper (Aloha-Agilex-1.0/2.0), dual-arm ARX5, dual-arm Franka-Panda, dual-arm UR5+UMI
headline_metric: task success rate vs. RDT / pi_0 / from-scratch (w/o human) ablation across sim and real platforms
headline_value: Dual-arm ARX5 few-shot (113 tasks, 1-5 demos/task): H-RDT 41.6% vs. RDT 16.0% vs. pi_0 31.2% vs. w/o-human 17.6% (Table 3); RoboTwin 2.0 multi-task (45 tasks, Hard mode): H-RDT 87.2% vs. RDT 28.8% vs. pi_0 48.4% vs. w/o-human 67.2% (Table 5)
human_data: EgoDex (existing public dataset, not self-collected): 829 hours, 338K+ trajectories across 194 manipulation tasks, with paired bilateral wrist pose + all-finger fingertip 3D-position annotations
note_gaps: no explicit Limitations section is present in the extracted text; the flow-matching vector-field loss equation is not fully recovered; combined average success for Aloha-Agilex-2.0 is stated inconsistently as 29.0% vs. 34% in different places
operator_interface: for pretraining: none (consumes EgoDex's pre-existing released 3D hand-pose annotations, no live capture by this paper); for fine-tuning: standard teleoperation of each robot platform, not described in detail
retargeting_objective: no explicit kinematic retargeting; the 48-D bimanual wrist+fingertip human action space is treated as a superset of most end-effector action spaces, and the human-to-robot correspondence is instead learned implicitly by reinitializing and fine-tuning the state/action adaptors and action decoder on paired robot data while keeping the pretrained vision/language backbone
